name: Cubbon Park, Bengaluru
notes: A large green space in the heart of Bengaluru, Cubbon Park is known for its dense tree cover, shaded walking paths and peaceful atmosphere. Some stretches feel surprisingly quiet despite being surrounded by the city.

name: MG Road Metro Station, Bengaluru
notes: One of Bengaluru’s busiest urban points, especially in the evening. The station brings together commuters, nearby shops, pedestrians and city traffic, making it an interesting place to experience the changing rhythm of the city.

name: HSR Layout Sector 2, Bengaluru
notes: HSR Layout is an interesting mix of residential streets, cafés, shops and newer commercial spaces. Exploring the neighbourhood reveals how quickly parts of Bengaluru are changing while pockets of open space still remain.

name: Sample Point A7
notes: Soil sample collected at 15cm depth. Slightly moist, dark brown. Logged for the land classification dataset.

name: Whitefield Tech Park Periphery, Bengaluru
notes: Rapid development is visible around the Whitefield tech park, with three new towers under construction since the last survey. The surrounding area is also experiencing increasing traffic congestion along the main access road. The combination of ongoing construction and growing traffic provides an interesting glimpse into how quickly this part of the city is changing.

name: Community Garden, Bengaluru
notes: A small urban farming space tucked into the neighbourhood. Vegetable beds and greenery create a refreshing contrast with the surrounding buildings, and it is easy to miss unless you take the time to look around.

name: Turahalli Forest Edge, Bengaluru
notes: The landscape changes quickly from Bengaluru's urban surroundings to scrub, rocky ground and narrow trails. The combination of natural terrain and distant city views makes this a memorable place for a short escape from the city.

name: Sample Point B3
notes: Water sample taken from the storm drain outlet. Slight discoloration and odor present. Flagged for lab testing alongside A7.

name: Malwa Plateau, Indore
notes: The Malwa Plateau is characterised by broad agricultural landscapes and the region's distinctive dark, fertile soil. The open fields and expansive views create a very different experience from the dense urban environments nearby.

name: Red Soil Landscape, Coimbatore
notes: The deep red soil gives this landscape its distinctive character. The contrast between the reddish earth, vegetation and open countryside makes the area particularly interesting to observe and photograph.

name: Chandni Chowk, Old Delhi
notes: One of Old Delhi's most distinctive areas, Chandni Chowk combines historic buildings, narrow lanes, markets, food and constant movement. Almost every turn reveals another small detail, shop or street scene worth remembering.

name: Howrah Riverside, Kolkata
notes: The riverside offers a different perspective of Kolkata, with the Hooghly, boats, buildings and everyday activity coming together in one constantly changing scene. It is an interesting place to slow down and simply observe the city.

name: Yamuna Expressway, Uttar Pradesh
notes: A six-lane access-controlled expressway forming an important transport corridor across Uttar Pradesh. Its wide roadway, controlled access and long stretches of open landscape make it an interesting example of large-scale transportation infrastructure and the way major road networks connect growing urban and regional areas.

name: Mumbai–Pune Expressway, Maharashtra
notes: The journey between Mumbai and Pune becomes especially memorable as the road passes through the Western Ghats. The changing scenery, hills and winding sections make the drive feel like part of the experience rather than simply a connection between two cities.

name: Varanasi Ghats
notes: The ghats along the Ganges are one of Varanasi's defining landscapes. Steps, temples, boats and daily rituals create a constantly changing riverfront, with a different atmosphere from morning to evening.

name: Amer Fort, Jaipur
notes: Perched on a hill overlooking the surrounding landscape, Amer Fort is a striking combination of courtyards, gateways, corridors and historic architecture. Exploring the complex reveals new views and details at almost every turn.

name: Hampi Ruins, Karnataka
notes: Hampi's historic ruins are scattered across an extraordinary landscape of massive boulders, hills and open spaces. Walking between temples and ancient structures makes the entire area feel like one enormous outdoor archaeological site.

name: Ashoka Pillar Site, Varanasi
notes: The Ashoka Pillar is a remarkable example of India's ancient stone inscriptions and imperial history. Seeing the carved details up close makes an otherwise distant period of history feel much more tangible.

name: Sarnath Museum Grounds, Varanasi
notes: Sarnath offers a quieter historical experience away from the busier parts of Varanasi. The museum surroundings, archaeological remains and open grounds create a peaceful setting for exploring the area's connection with India's ancient history.

name: Varanasi Ring Road Junction
notes: Newly widened junction, moderate traffic during peak hours.

name: Rann of Kutch Salt Flats, Gujarat
notes: The Rann of Kutch is known for its vast white salt landscape, which can appear almost endless under the open sky. The unusual terrain, enormous scale and lack of visual clutter make it an especially memorable place for exploration and photography.

name: Old Bakery, Pune
notes: A small neighbourhood bakery away from the main road, where the smell of freshly baked food becomes part of the experience. Places like this can reveal a more everyday side of a neighbourhood, especially when they have been serving local residents for years. It is the kind of discovery worth remembering for a future walk through the area.

name: Riverside Spot, Pune
notes: A simple riverside location where reflections, moving water, surrounding buildings and changing light create different photographic opportunities throughout the day. Early morning and evening can give the scene a completely different atmosphere, making it worth revisiting at different times.

name: Sabarmati Riverfront, Ahmedabad
notes: A landscaped waterfront along the Sabarmati River, offering views of the river, bridges, promenades and Ahmedabad's urban skyline. The changing light and reflections on the water create different photographic opportunities throughout the day, particularly around sunrise and sunset.

name: Manali, Himachal Pradesh
notes: A Himalayan destination surrounded by mountains, forests and the Beas River, with access to activities such as trekking, paragliding, skiing and river rafting. Nearby Solang Valley and the routes toward higher Himalayan terrain make the surrounding landscape particularly suited to outdoor exploration.

name: Rishikesh, Uttarakhand
notes: A well-known adventure destination along the Ganges, particularly associated with white-water rafting and other outdoor activities. The combination of the river, surrounding hills and access to the Himalayan foothills makes the area suitable for experiences that involve both exploration and physical activity.

name: Hawa Mahal, Jaipur
notes: The iconic pink façade of Hawa Mahal provides one of Jaipur's most recognizable photographic scenes. Its rows of small windows, intricate architecture and changing light create different compositions throughout the day, particularly around sunrise and the softer evening hours.

name: Manek Chowk, Ahmedabad
notes: A lively food market in the heart of Ahmedabad's old city, known for its street-food stalls and vibrant atmosphere, particularly after sunset. The area offers a mix of traditional Gujarati snacks, local favourites and late-night food, making it a memorable place to experience Ahmedabad's everyday food culture.

name: Gateway of India, Mumai
notes: An iconic waterfront landmark overlooking Mumbai Harbour. The monument, Arabian Sea, surrounding boats and historic buildings create several different photographic compositions, particularly around sunrise, sunset and the evening blue hour.

name: Kachori Gali, Varanasi
notes: A narrow and lively food street in the old part of Varanasi, known for traditional kachoris, jalebi and lassi. The compact lanes, small food shops and constant movement create an experience that reflects the everyday food culture of the city.

name: Bahubali Hills, Udaipur, Rajasthan
notes: A scenic hilltop overlooking the surrounding landscape near Udaipur, with open views of the hills and lake-filled terrain. The climb and elevated viewpoint offer a peaceful setting away from the city, while the changing light across the landscape makes the location especially appealing during sunrise and sunset.

name: Kedarnath Temple, Uttarakhand
notes: A historic Himalayan temple dedicated to Lord Shiva, located at an elevation of around 3,570 metres in the Kedarnath region of Uttarakhand. Surrounded by dramatic mountain landscapes, the temple is an important pilgrimage site and forms part of the cultural and religious heritage of the Himalayas.

name: Somnath Temple, Gujarat
notes: A prominent Shiva temple on the coast of Gujarat and one of the traditionally recognized Jyotirlinga pilgrimage sites. Its long history, repeated reconstruction and distinctive coastal setting make it an important part of Gujarat's religious and architectural heritage.

name: Dagdusheth Halwai Ganapati Temple, Pune
notes: A famous Ganapati temple in the heart of Pune, known for its ornate idol and its connection with the city's long-standing Ganesh festival traditions. Established in the late 19th century, the temple has become an important part of Pune's cultural identity and attracts large numbers of devotees during Ganeshotsav.

name: Jagannath Temple, Puri, Odisha
notes: A historic temple dedicated to Lord Jagannath and one of the most important pilgrimage centres in Odisha. The temple is closely associated with the annual Rath Yatra, in which the deities are carried through the streets of Puri on large wooden chariots. Its Kalinga-style architecture and continuing cultural traditions make it a significant part of Odisha's heritage.
